why: An instance method in the heap core takes `this` as a reference to the record of the class's fields: add writes a different count (unproved; lane B's programs on a constructed instance witness it at the first command); grow names the fields through locals and reads the size in place of calling size(), the same reads and writes in the same order (proved; lane B traces a receiver's field reads, so the refactor keeps their order); size and total are untouched (proved). The constructor stays outside the core and keeps its ordinary reading.
